turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Probably nothing, but I have deliberately skipped eating for two days to make the scales move faster. I feel awkward saying that because I know it is different from just being less hungry, and I don't want the message to come across like I am asking you to praise it. I kept thinking I would mention it another time, then decided that leaving it out wasn't very useful if I wanted the clinic to understand what was happening. I don't want a detailed food plan in the chat. I would like to know who I can speak to about it without having to pretend it was accidental.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Thank you for being honest, Chris. You don't need to pretend it was accidental. Going without food like this is worth talking through with a clinician. I'll arrange a prescriber review, with a reply within 2 working days.

I don't want to write a long explanation that tries to justify everything, because the important thing is what I actually did and why. I can tell the prescriber the same thing I have told you here, and I don't need to make it more dramatic or less serious than it was. turns.speaker: responder

turns.text: Hi Aisha, smaller portions can make eating out feel more manageable. You could choose an entrée-sized meal or set some aside, and eat at a comfortable pace.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Hi Rangi, walking is a useful way to build regular movement, especially when it's something you enjoy. General activity guidance also includes strength activities on at least 2 days a week, which can be done at home.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: but i really dont want equipment and all that

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: You don't need a gym to start. Simple strength activities such as standing up from a chair can fit alongside walking. We can choose a small, manageable starting goal together.
